newsitem.title: ITALY: Ambroveneto still to assess BancoNapoli.
newsitem.headline: Ambroveneto still to assess BancoNapoli.

text.p: Italy's Banco Ambrosiano Veneto said its board had not started to evaluate taking a possible stake in troubled Banco di Napoli.
The Italy Treasury announced earlier this week that it is looking to sell an initial 60 percent chunk of southern Italy's largest bank based in Naples.
"We will possibily present our shareholders with a plan," Ambroveneto's managing director Corrado Passera told journalists while attending a financial conference.
Passera added that the privatisation process had now started, and when his bank receives material next week from the privatisation advisors, then Ambroveneto may present a plan to its shareholders.
He said that at the moment Ambroveneto was interested in Banco di Napoli, but had no fixed plans.

The next board meeting of Ambroveneto is set for October 29, while potential buyers have until November 18 to declare an interest in the sale and will then be given until December 20 to make a final offer.
